ai.title: PlacementTotals adds deliverySpendCents for rate metrics
ai.summary: PlacementTotals in common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts adds deliverySpendCents to separate ledger-billed spend from delivery-charged spend. Rate metrics now divide by deliverySpendCents to prevent manual back-bills from skewing eCPC and eCPM. This change affects core constants and placement totals interfaces.

eli5.text: When the system calculates how much each ad click or thousand impressions actually cost you, it now separates two different numbers: what the billing ledger says you were charged versus what the delivery rows themselves recorded as charged. Previously, a manual back-bill or adjustment line in the ledger would sneak into the cost-per-click and cost-per-impression ratios, pulling them away from the real per-action price. Rate metrics now divide by the delivery-charged spend field, so manual ledger-only corrections no longer distort the average costs shown in reports. The new field is added alongside the existing spend total, so any report or dashboard that reads placement totals can opt into the cleaner rate numbers.

ai.title: GLM 5.3 Flash becomes the default free model across CLI, Web
ai.summary: GLM 5.3 Flash (`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`) replaces GPT-5.6 Luna as `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID` and `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, and `GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL` is reordered to the front of `FREEBUFF_MODELS` so every picker leads with it. Because this row is unmetered and uncapped, the `premiumExhausted` step-down in `getRecommendedFreebuffModelId` and `getRecommendedFreebuffWebModelId` is now gated behind `isFreebuffPremiumModelId`, so a spent premium pool no longer forces a new user off the recommended hero. The three README surfaces were rewritten to match the new default and the removal of GLM 5.3 Flash's 2-sessions-a-day cap.

README.md, README.zh-CN.md, and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md` update the model tables and FAQ text to match.
ai.unknowns: The rollout date for the new default to reach end-user clients is not visible in the diff.

changes.what: GLM 5.3 Flash becomes the default model for CLI/Desktop and Web/Cloud by switching DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID and DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID, and it is reordered to the top of FREEBUFF_MODELS.

The premiumExhausted step-down in getRecommendedFreebuffModelId and getRecommendedFreebuffWebModelId is now guarded by isFreebuffPremiumModelId so the unmetered default is no longer stepped off a spent pool.
README.md, README.zh-CN.md, and freebuff/cli/release/README.md update the model tables, default descriptions, and FAQ text to reflect GLM 5.3 Flash as the default and its new unmetered status.

ai.title: Freebuff session hook re-resolves saved model by subscription tier
ai.summary: Two exports were added to cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts: resolveFreebuffModelPickForSession routes an explicit picker action through resolveFreebuffModelForAccessTier with the server's tierId verdict, and resolveFreebuffModelSelectionForSession reconciles the picker on a fresh session response. startFreebuffSession now calls resolveFreebuffModelPickForSession instead of reading accessTier and calling resolveFreebuffModelForAccessTier inline. The apply callback replaced the old 'none'+limited coercion to LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID with resolveFreebuffModelSelectionForSession, so a limited-access subscriber keeps their saved plan model selected instead of being pinned to the free tier id. This keeps the picker's tier-aware offer in lockstep with session admission so saved premium-row picks survive the transition.
ai.evidence: cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts: added resolveFreebuffModelPickForSession and resolveFreebuffModelSelectionForSession, and replaced the inline accessTier lookup and resolveFreebuffModelForAccessTier call in startFreebuffSession with a call to resolveFreebuffModelPickForSession; in the apply callback the previous 'none'/limited branch that coerced to LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID was replaced by resolveFreebuffModelSelectionForSession.

ai.title: Derived ad credit line constants added for COD-268
ai.summary: The commit introduces the constant set that will back an advertiser trust score / derived credit line (COD-268) in `common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts`, the shared placements prepayment module. The line is modeled as days of observed burn rather than a multiple of the 30-day spend total, with growth clamped to at most doubling the live line and decreases clamped to 25 percent per run, matching the existing CPC repricer guard. These are pure declarations with no consumer in the diff, so they configure the rulebook the advertiser-facing form and the webhook-side parser must agree on, deferring enforcement to a later change.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a new block of exports in `common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts` (lines 63-89): `AD_CREDIT_LINE_WINDOW_DAYS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MIN_DAYS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MAX_DAYS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_CEILING_CENTS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MIN_ACCOUNT_AGE_DAYS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MIN_SUCCESSFUL_COLLECTIONS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MAX_GROWTH_BPS`, `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MIN_GROWTH_STEP_CENTS`, and `AD_CREDIT_LINE_MAX_DECREASE_BPS`, all under a comment tagged COD-268. No reader of these constants appears in the diff.
